question_text: A chemical refinery produces two blends, Blend P and Blend Q, by mixing three base solutions: A, B, and C. Blend P must contain at least 40% of Solution A and at most 30% of Solution C by volume. Blend Q must contain at least 25% of Solution B and no more than 50% of Solution C by volume. The refinery has 400 liters of A, 300 liters of B, and 350 liters of C available. The profit per liter is $5 for Blend P and $4 for Blend Q. To maximize profit, the refinery wants to use as much of the available base solutions as possible, without exceeding the available volumes, while strictly adhering to the blend composition constraints. If x represents the total volume (in liters) of Blend P produced and y represents the total volume (in liters) of Blend Q produced, which of the following systems of inequalities correctly represents the constraints on x and y for this maximization problem?
